physics-killer-05.goal: Analyze the underlying scientific principles and deduce the correct conclusion.
physics-killer-05.material: An object of mass $2\,\mathrm{kg}$ is moving in the $+x$ direction at $4\,\mathrm{m/s}$. A force in the $+x$ direction acts on it: its magnitude rises uniformly from $0$ to $40\,\mathrm{N}$ during $0$ to $0.1\,\mathrm{s}$, stays constant at $40\,\mathrm{N}$ during $0.1$ to $0.3\,\mathrm{s}$, and falls uniformly from $40\,\mathrm{N}$ to $0$ during $0.3$ to $0.4\,\mathrm{s}$. Which option correctly gives, in order, the magnitude of the impulse the object receives during these $0.4\,\mathrm{s}$ and its speed just after the force disappears? (There are no other forces.)
physics-killer-05.thinking.0: Collisions and Safety, Horizontal Projection and Gravity
physics-killer-05.s.s1.prompt: An object of mass $2\,\mathrm{kg}$ is moving in the $+x$ direction at $4\,\mathrm{m/s}$. A force in the $+x$ direction acts on it: its magnitude rises uniformly from $0$ to $40\,\mathrm{N}$ during $0$ to $0.1\,\mathrm{s}$, stays constant at $40\,\mathrm{N}$ during $0.1$ to $0.3\,\mathrm{s}$, and falls uniformly from $40\,\mathrm{N}$ to $0$ during $0.3$ to $0.4\,\mathrm{s}$. Which option correctly gives, in order, the magnitude of the impulse the object receives during these $0.4\,\mathrm{s}$ and its speed just after the force disappears? (There are no other forces.)
physics-killer-05.s.s1.explain: Areas: first triangle $\frac12\cdot0.1\cdot40=2$, rectangle $0.2\cdot40=8$, last triangle $2$, so $I=12\,\mathrm{N\cdot s}$. From $I=m(v-v_0)$, $12=2(v-4)\Rightarrow v=10\,\mathrm{m/s}$. Treating the whole graph as a rectangle $40\cdot0.4=16$ gives option 2; omitting the triangles and using $8$ gives option 3; not dividing $I$ by the mass and writing $4+12=16$ gives option 4.
